issues.detail: The Hebrew says 'the sons of Dishan' (בְּנֵי דִישָׁן), but the Chinese renders '底善人的兒子' which adds 人 ('people of Dishan') and then lists '黑馬丹人' (Hemdan people) with 人 added, whereas the Hebrew has no 人 on the names. More importantly, the Hebrew names are חֶמְדָּן (Hemdan), אֶשְׁבָּן (Eshban), יִתְרָן (Yithran), כְרָן (Keran); the Chinese gives 黑馬丹人 (Hemdan), 以實班 (Eshban), 益蘭 (Yithran), 基蘭 (Keran) — the first name has an unwarranted 人 suffix, and the others are acceptable transliterations. The main issue is the added 人 on '底善人' and '黑馬丹人', which changes the meaning from 'sons of Dishan' to 'people of Dishan' and 'Hemdan people'.
